newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end mixed as budget delivered.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end mixed as budget delivered.

text.p: Singapore shares closed mixed on Friday with selective stocks staging a rebound as the budget was being unveiled.
Earlier, the effective devaluation of the Philippine peso weighed on the exchange as foreign funds stayed away from the region, brokers said.
The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended off 1.20 points at 1,967.14, after trading in a tight 1,962.72-1,969.87 range.
The budget which was still being delivered by Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu had no immediate impact with brokers saying they were still absorbing his speech.
"The focus is on those markets whose currencies are under attack. We're still listening to Hu," one said.
Another broker said the budget speech appearred "unexciting."
DBS Land led the rebound in property stocks, up Singapore $0.16 (US$0.11) to S$4.70 on 3.1 million shares.
A few speculative counters saw buying interest in the afternoon.
Raffles Medical Group rose to S$1.21 with a gain of S$0.09 on 4.5 million shares as rumours of a takeover made another round in the market.
The over-the-counter index measuring mostly Malaysian stocks finished 2.84 points up at 1,102.72, lifted by a positive reversal in the Kuala Lumpur market.
Total volume was 151.76 million shares with gainers outpacing losers by 260 to 100.
